note: Frigate tuna. Often sold as palamut at fish markets. Distinguished by spots (vs lines on palamut), no teeth, and darker meat.

name: Mazzancolla
note: Premium Mediterranean prawn, also called gambero imperiale

name: Calamaro
note: Common squid; the word spread to Arabic as كلماري and Turkish as kalamar

name: Ombrina
note: Prized table fish, also called corvo di mare (sea raven)

name: Leccia
note: Fast-swimming predator, popular game fish

name: Scorfano nero
note: Small scorpionfish with venomous spines; essential for Mediterranean fish soup

name: Grongo
note: Large marine eel, used in fish soups

name: Capone
note: Gurnard with distinctive large head; Greek Καπόνι is borrowed from this

name: Acciuga
note: European anchovy; source of Arabic أنشوفة (via Mediterranean trade)

name: Dentice corazziere
note: Named for helmet-like bony hump on head; corazziere refers to armored cavalry

name: Corbèl
note: Venetian name for shi drum; the fish makes a drumming sound

name: Större kungsfisk
note: Literally "larger kingfish". Also called rödfisk (redfish) or uer.

name: Golden redfish
note: Also called rose fish, ocean perch, Norway haddock

name: Puna-ahven
note: Commercial name variant

name: Anglerfish
note: Also called Monkfish

name: γόγγρος
note: Source of Latin conger and modern Italian grongo. Attested in Aristotle.

name: Turkish salmon
note: Not commercially farmed in Turkey. "Turkish salmon" marketed in Turkey is actually sea-grown rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), not Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar). Turkey is the largest producer of rainbow trout.

name: Çupra
note: Historically older form (1876 Ottoman attestation). Dominant colloquial form in İzmir/Aegean coast.

name: Çıpra
note: Rare variant. Poorly attested in major references — absent from Nişanyan Sözlük, TDK, FishBase, and Wikidata.

name: Sarpa
note: Borrowed via Ottoman-era Greek fishing communities. The r-variant (σάρπα) rather than l-variant (σάλπα) entered Turkish.

name: Müren balığı
note: Literally moray fish. Found along Turkish Mediterranean and Aegean coasts.
